stem: In the Sikh wedding rite, Anand Karaj, the four lavan sung as the couple walks around the Guru Granth Sahib were composed by which Guru?
options: Guru Amar Das, the third Guru
Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru
Guru Ram Das, the fourth Guru
Guru Nanak Dev, the first Guru
why: The lavan are four verses of Guru Ram Das in Rag Suhi; at each one the couple makes a round of the Guru Granth Sahib. The Anand Marriage Act of 1909 gave weddings by this rite legal standing. Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 773-774.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Rag Suhi, Mahala 4, Ang 773-774; Anand Marriage Act, 1909

es.stem: En el rito de boda sij, el Anand Karaj, ¿qué Gurú compuso las cuatro lavan que se cantan mientras la pareja camina alrededor del Gurú Granth Sahib?
options: Gurú Amar Das, el tercer Gurú
Gurú Arjan Dev, el quinto Gurú
Gurú Ram Das, el cuarto Gurú
Gurú Nanak Dev, el primer Gurú
es.why: Las lavan son cuatro versos de Gurú Ram Das en el Rag Suhi; con cada una, la pareja da una vuelta alrededor del Gurú Granth Sahib. La Ley de Matrimonio Anand de 1909 dio validez legal a las bodas con este rito. Gurú Granth Sahib, Ang 773-774.

stem: In the Nankana Sahib massacre of February 1921, which leader of a band of gurdwara reformers does Sikh memory say was tied to a jand tree and burned?
options: Bhai Lachhman Singh
Baba Kharak Singh
Master Tara Singh
Professor Teja Singh
why: Bhai Lachhman Singh led a jatha into the gurdwara at Guru Nanak's birthplace; the mahant Narain Das's men attacked the reciting reformers, and Sikh memory holds that the wounded Lachhman Singh was tied to the jand tree that still stands there and burned.
source: Gurdwara reform movement: Saka Nankana Sahib, 20 February 1921

es.stem: En la masacre de Nankana Sahib de febrero de 1921, ¿a qué líder de un grupo de reformistas de los gurdwaras, según la memoria sij, ataron a un árbol jand y quemaron?
options: Bhai Lachhman Singh
Baba Kharak Singh
Master Tara Singh
el profesor Teja Singh
es.why: Bhai Lachhman Singh encabezó un jatha que entró al gurdwara del lugar de nacimiento de Gurú Nanak; los hombres del mahant Narain Das atacaron a los reformistas mientras recitaban, y la memoria sij cuenta que a Lachhman Singh, herido, lo ataron al árbol jand que aún sigue allí y lo quemaron.

stem: In 1913 an outer wall of Gurdwara Rakab Ganj in Delhi was torn down to make way for the new capital. Why is that ground so sacred to Sikhs?
options: It is where Guru Tegh Bahadur was beheaded in 1675
It is where Guru Tegh Bahadur's body was cremated
It is where Guru Har Krishan tended the sick of Delhi
It is where Mata Sundari lived after leaving Anandpur
why: After Guru Tegh Bahadur's execution in 1675 (at the site of Gurdwara Sis Ganj), Lakhi Shah Vanjara carried his body away and cremated it by setting fire to his own house; Gurdwara Rakab Ganj stands there. Sikh protest led to the wall being rebuilt.
source: Sikh tradition of Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom; Rakab Ganj wall agitation, 1913-1920

es.stem: En 1913 se derribó un muro exterior del Gurdwara Rakab Ganj, en Delhi, para abrir paso a la nueva capital. ¿Por qué ese terreno es tan sagrado para los sijs?
options: Es donde decapitaron a Gurú Tegh Bahadur en 1675
Es donde se cremó el cuerpo de Gurú Tegh Bahadur
Es donde Gurú Har Krishan atendió a los enfermos de Delhi
Es donde vivió Mata Sundari después de dejar Anandpur
es.why: Tras la ejecución de Gurú Tegh Bahadur en 1675 (en el sitio del Gurdwara Sis Ganj), Lakhi Shah Vanjara se llevó su cuerpo y lo cremó prendiendo fuego a su propia casa; allí se alza el Gurdwara Rakab Ganj. La protesta sij logró que el muro se reconstruyera.

stem: In the 1921-22 'keys affair', how did Sikhs win back the keys of the toshakhana (treasury) of the Golden Temple, Harmandir Sahib, from the British government?
options: through a ruling of the Lahore High Court
through a payment raised by the sangat
through an appeal by the Maharaja of Patiala
through peaceful protest and mass arrests
why: When an official took the treasury keys into government hands, Sikhs answered with nonviolent meetings and protest; leaders such as Baba Kharak Singh and many volunteers were jailed, until the government released them and handed the keys to Kharak Singh in January 1922.
source: Gurdwara reform movement: the keys affair (Chabian da Morcha), 1921-22

es.stem: En el 'asunto de las llaves' de 1921-22, ¿cómo recuperaron los sijs, del gobierno británico, las llaves del toshakhana (tesoro) del Templo Dorado, Harmandir Sahib?
options: con un fallo del Tribunal Superior de Lahore
con un pago reunido entre toda la sangat
con una petición del maharajá de Patiala
con protesta pacífica y arrestos masivos
es.why: Cuando un funcionario puso las llaves del tesoro en manos del gobierno, los sijs respondieron con reuniones y protestas no violentas; encarcelaron a líderes como Baba Kharak Singh y a muchos voluntarios, hasta que el gobierno los liberó y entregó las llaves a Kharak Singh en enero de 1922.

stem: In the Sikh story recalled each Maghi at Muktsar, why does Guru Gobind Singh tear up the bedava, the letter in which a band of Sikhs disowned him?
options: The Mughal governor had sworn to grant them safe passage
The men who signed it came back and died defending him
Mai Bhago had paid a fine on the deserters' behalf
The signers had all taken amrit again at Anandpur
why: The Sikhs who had signed the bedava at Anandpur, stirred by Mai Bhago, returned and fell at Khidrana in 1705; the dying Mahan Singh asked the Guru to forgive them, and he tore the paper. The Ardas remembers them as the Chali Mukte, the forty liberated ones.
source: Sikh tradition of the Chali Mukte, battle of Khidrana (Muktsar), 1705; Ardas

es.stem: En la historia sij que se recuerda cada Maghi en Muktsar, ¿por qué Gurú Gobind Singh rompe el bedava, la carta en que un grupo de sijs renegó de él?
options: El gobernador mogol les había jurado un paso seguro
Los firmantes volvieron y murieron defendiéndolo
Mai Bhago había pagado una multa por los desertores
Los firmantes habían vuelto a tomar amrit en Anandpur
es.why: Los sijs que firmaron el bedava en Anandpur, movidos por Mai Bhago, volvieron y cayeron en Khidrana en 1705; Mahan Singh, moribundo, le pidió al Gurú que los perdonara, y él rompió el papel. La Ardas los recuerda como los Chali Mukte, los cuarenta liberados.

stem: The hereditary custodian of a historic gurdwara listed under the Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925 says he may pass the shrine to his son. Under the Act, who oversees the shrine's management instead?
options: a manager named by the Punjab government
the son, once the town's sangat agrees
a board whose members Sikh voters elect
the Jathedar of the Akal Takht alone
why: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925 ended hereditary control of the gurdwaras it lists and placed their management under a Sikh body elected by Sikh voters, the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC).

es.stem: El custodio hereditario de un gurdwara histórico incluido en la Ley de Gurdwaras Sijs de 1925 dice que puede dejarle el santuario a su hijo. Según la ley, ¿quién supervisa en cambio la administración del santuario?
options: un administrador nombrado por el gobierno del Panyab
el hijo, si la sangat del pueblo está de acuerdo
una junta cuyos miembros eligen los votantes sijs
el Jathedar del Akal Takht, por su propia cuenta
es.why: La Ley de Gurdwaras Sijs de 1925 puso fin al control hereditario de los gurdwaras que incluye y dejó su administración en manos de un organismo sij elegido por votantes sijs, el Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC).

stem: What is the Sikh Rehat Maryada, and how did it come to be written?
why: The Sikh Rehat Maryada is the code of Sikh conduct and conventions issued by the SGPC: it defines who a Sikh is and sets out personal practice, gurdwara practice and the rites of life. Committees of scholars and leaders drafted and revised it from the early 1930s; it was approved in 1945 and published around 1950.

rubric.point: Says it is the Sikh code of conduct (rehat), covering personal life and practice in the gurdwara, such as prayers, rites of birth, marriage and death, langar or amrit. Calling it 'a rule book' with no sense of what it covers counts as partly.

Says it was drafted over years by committees of Sikh scholars and leaders under the SGPC (from the 1930s, approved in 1945, published around 1950). 'The SGPC wrote it' with no sense of a long, shared drafting process counts as partly; saying a Guru wrote it does not count.
Mentions its definition of a Sikh: faith in the One Immortal Being, the ten Gurus, the Guru Granth Sahib and the amrit of the tenth Guru (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: ¿Qué es el Sikh Rehat Maryada y cómo se llegó a escribir?
es.why: El Sikh Rehat Maryada es el código de conducta y costumbres sijs que publica el SGPC: define quién es sij y describe la práctica personal, la práctica en el gurdwara y los ritos de la vida. Comités de eruditos y líderes lo redactaron y revisaron desde principios de los años treinta; se aprobó en 1945 y se publicó hacia 1950.

stem: Who was Bhagat Puran Singh, and what did he found in Amritsar?
why: Puran Singh, a sevadar at a Lahore gurdwara, took in an abandoned disabled boy, Piara, and carried and cared for him for years; after Partition in 1947 he crossed to Amritsar with him and began the Pingalwara, a home for the disabled, destitute and dying that still runs there.
source: Life of Bhagat Puran Singh (1904-1992); All India Pingalwara Charitable Society, Amritsar

rubric.point: Names the Pingalwara, or describes a home in Amritsar for disabled, abandoned, destitute or dying people. 'A charity' with no sense of who it serves counts as partly.
Says his work began with caring for an abandoned disabled boy (Piara) whom he carried on his back for years, or that he was a volunteer (sevadar) living a life of seva. Either counts.
Mentions that he came to Amritsar as a refugee at Partition in 1947, or that people gave him the name Bhagat, devotee (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: ¿Quién fue Bhagat Puran Singh y qué fundó en Amritsar?
es.why: Puran Singh, sevadar en un gurdwara de Lahore, acogió a un niño con discapacidad abandonado, Piara, y lo cargó y cuidó durante años; tras la Partición de 1947 cruzó con él a Amritsar y comenzó el Pingalwara, un hogar para personas con discapacidad, sin recursos o moribundas que todavía funciona allí.
